subject: mathematics
question_text: In a △ABC, show that r + r₃ + r₁ − r₂ = 4R cos B.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.76 — SAQ chapter 13 Properties of Triangles, answer 84.2, on a ★★★ SSP (Super Scoring Page). Printed appearances: AP 18,22. The twin of 84.1. Same method, but the pairs are chosen around B instead of C — and the answer keeps a cos B because the angles do not sum to 180° inside the bracket this time. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed against this answer. It is not a bare guess: the same book prints 1+1+1+1 for the 4-mark answers 58 and 59 on book p.63 and 1+2+1 for answer 61 on p.64, so both shapes used in this unit are the book's own. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B runs Q11-Q17 at 4 marks each, answer any 5 of 7; Q17 is the Properties of Triangles slot. Together with Q24 (LAQ) this unit holds TWO slots — one of only two units to do so, Matrices being the other.

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name each standard result you use and the order you use them in.

steps.label: Group into two pairs
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. Group (r₃ + r₁) and (r − r₂), which share 4R cos(B/2) and 4R sin(B/2) — the B half-angle, since B is what the answer keeps.
steps.memory_tip: Group (r₃ + r₁) and (r − r₂) — they share the B half-angle, which is what the answer keeps.

recall.must_convey: That the four radii are grouped as (r₃+r₁) and (r−r₂), factoring out 4R cos(B/2) and 4R sin(B/2).
accept: group r three plus r one and r minus r two then take four R cos half B and four R sin half B out
pair them around B this time
the common factors are the B half angles
B chuttu group cheyyali, cos half B and sin half B common
group so the B half angle factors out

steps.why: The answer keeps a cos B, so the grouping must leave B behind rather than cancel it — which is why the pairs are chosen around B and not C.
common_mistakes: Copying the twin and grouping around C.
Losing the minus in front of the second group.

steps.label: Apply the compound formulas
steps.margin_note: The other half. The brackets become sin((A+C)/2) and cos((A+C)/2); then (A+C)/2 = 90° − B/2 turns both into B, and cos²−sin² gives cos B.
steps.memory_tip: (A + C)/2 = 90° − B/2 turns both brackets into B, and cos² − sin² gives cos B.

lines.text: = 4R cos B = R.H.S   [∵ cos2θ = cos²θ − sin²θ]

recall.must_convey: That sin((A+C)/2) = cos(B/2) and cos((A+C)/2) = sin(B/2), giving 4R[cos²(B/2) − sin²(B/2)] = 4R cos B.
accept: sin of half A plus C is cos half B so it becomes four R cos squared minus sin squared which is four R cos B
use the complementary angle then the double angle formula
cos squared half B minus sin squared half B is cos B
A plus C by two ante ninety minus B by two, so cos half B vasthundi
the difference of squares gives cos B

steps.why: cos²θ − sin²θ = cos 2θ, and here θ is B/2 — so the answer is cos B exactly. That is why the B half-angles had to be the ones factored out.

insider_note: Group as (r₃ + r₁) and (r − r₂) so that cos(B/2) and sin(B/2) come out as factors. (A+C)/2 = 90° − B/2 is the substitution that makes both brackets collapse.
